item.title: Budget Analyst (Recent Graduate)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 8/12/2026.

The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) within the Department of Commerce is hiring a Budget Analyst (Recent Graduate) at the GS-7 level through the Pathways Recent Graduate Program. Applicants must have completed, within the previous two years, a qualifying degree or certificate from an accredited educational institution (veterans may have up to six years). GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale is required. U.S. citizenship required. Upon completion of the minimum one-year career development program, participants may be non-competitively converted to a permanent or term position at agency discretion (conversion is not guaranteed). Apply via USAJOBS.

Key responsibilities include: preparing initial budget estimates and justifications for assigned areas or programs in accordance with standard operating procedures; performing budget formulation, execution, and administration work involving the monitoring of obligations incurred and actual expenditures of funds; comparing obligations and expenditures to identify conditions of over or under obligation; assisting with reviewing and performing initial analysis of budget estimates and requests for allotments submitted by managers; reviewing organizational historical data and matching funding requests to determine trends in spending and forecast annual funding needs; and analyzing budget estimates and narratives for reasonableness and adequacy as it relates to increases, decreases, or changes in project scope or outcome.

Qualifications: completed within the previous two years a qualifying associate's, bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate, vocational or technical degree or certificate from an accredited institution; GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale; U.S. citizenship required; and meet one of: completion of one full academic year of graduate level education in a related field; Superior Academic Achievement (upper third of graduating class, GPA 3.0+, or national scholastic honor society membership); one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05 including assisting with gathering budget information, performing initial analysis of budget estimates, and tracking obligations and expenditures; or a combination of education and experience.

Compensation and logistics: GS-7 pay scale (base range approximately $49,000-$64,000 annually depending on location). Federal benefits including health insurance, retirement, TSP, and paid leave. Washington, DC area. Recent Graduate Program appointment; conversion to permanent or term position not guaranteed.

Key responsibilities include: leading state-level program implementation; coordinating and developing partnerships with diverse leaders across New York State; guiding and facilitating the engagement of leaders into Resilient States programming including collaborative action to prevent, defuse, and respond to risks for political violence; supporting delivery of training and tools; serving as primary representation for CG-USA at the state level; developing state program in coordination with national strategy; providing inputs to strategy development and planning; supervising one or more state-level staff; and overseeing internal operational processes for state activities.

Qualifications: a BS/BA with a minimum of 11 years of experience; minimum 2 years of leadership experience highly desired; deep knowledge of and relationships with civil society and community leaders in New York; demonstrated ability to work with partners from different backgrounds and viewpoints; experience in broad-based coalition building highly desired; and a commitment to working across difference to build a more peaceful and just America.

The League of California Cities (Cal Cities), headquartered in downtown Sacramento since 1898, is an active partner in local government working to expand and protect local control for cities through education and advocacy to enhance the quality of life for all Californians. item.description:

Bread for the World is a Christian advocacy organization urging U.S. decision makers to do all they can to pursue a world without hunger through education and advocacy on policies and programs related to ending hunger in the U.S. and around the world. The International Policy Fellow is a two-year, time-limited full-time fellowship supporting the Government Relations team in advancing U.S. international development, global health, nutrition, and humanitarian policy. The fellow will work closely with the Senior International Policy Analyst and Government Relations leadership, gaining practical experience in policy research, legislative advocacy, coalition building, and strategic engagement with Congress, the Executive Branch, and leading faith-based and humanitarian organizations. Note: as appropriate and assigned, the fellow may be required to register as a lobbyist. The position is based in Washington, DC and is hybrid. Commitment to Bread for the World's Christian mission and advocacy approach is required.

Key responsibilities include: conducting policy research and analyzing legislative and regulatory developments related to global health, humanitarian assistance, food security, nutrition, and international development including programs such as PEPFAR, Gavi, and other U.S. foreign assistance priorities; supporting the development and execution of advocacy strategies with Congress, the White House, federal agencies, and coalition partners; potentially registering as a lobbyist and representing Bread for the World on Capitol Hill; coordinating high-level congressional meetings, listening sessions, and issue briefings; monitoring congressional activity, committee actions, appropriations, and authorizing legislation; representing Bread in coalition meetings, working groups, and policy forums; and preparing policy updates, briefings, and written materials for Bread staff, advocates, churches, and coalition partners.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in political science, international relations, public policy, international development, public health, or a related field; demonstrated interest in international development, global health, humanitarian assistance, or anti-hunger policy; excellent research, analytical, and writing skills; and commitment to Bread for the World's Christian mission and advocacy approach. Preferred: master's degree; internship or professional experience on Capitol Hill, within the Executive Branch, or an advocacy organization; and strong grasp of congressional processes.

Compensation and logistics: salary $50,000-$55,000 annually. Two-year time-limited fellowship. Hybrid in Washington, DC. Some evening and weekend hours required.

item.title: Research Assistant, Economic Studies
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 8/12/2026.

The Brookings Institution is a nonprofit public policy organization based in Washington, DC whose mission is to equip decision-makers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies. The Economic Studies program analyzes current and emerging economic issues facing the United States and the world, covering economic growth, economic opportunity and mobility, the labor market, regulation, health policy, the environment, tax policy, retirement policy, and fiscal and monetary policy. The Research Assistant supports scholars conducting research and policy analysis on global trade and capital flows and the policies that shape them, with a particular focus on their role in geopolitics and economic statecraft. Note: this position is included in the staff bargaining unit, Brookings United, affiliated with the IFPTE Local 70 union. A complete application requires a current resume, cover letter, and a copy of the latest unofficial undergraduate transcript. Hybrid in Washington, DC (two days remote per week). Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

Key responsibilities include (45%): quantitative analysis, programming, and statistical support -- working jointly with senior scholars on research projects including preparing and revising programming code, simulation macros, database files, and regression estimates; creating charts and graphs; developing statistical analysis; and assembling, consolidating, and checking data from new sources. (35%): research support -- drafting material summarizing research results, providing analytical reviews and summaries of existing literature, locating and analyzing relevant documents and data from electronic databases and government publications, and maintaining electronic bibliography files. (10%): office and administrative support -- scheduling, organizing files, composing and editing documents, and responding to inquiries. (5%): event planning support and (5%): communications and outreach.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in economics, mathematics/statistics, public policy, or other social sciences with a minor in economics required; competence to undertake research assignments with little supervision; experience with STATA, R, or other econometric packages required; Microsoft Office experience required; and experience with data visualization tools such as Datawrapper and Tableau preferred.

Compensation and logistics: projected hiring salary $58,000. Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Hybrid in Washington, DC (two days remote per week). Cover letter and unofficial transcript required.

The Communications & Policy Associate/Manager will help conduct policy research, analysis, writing, and advocacy on social or structural determinants of health issues, particularly affordable housing, workforce development, and food security/systems, while also managing HAN's communications strategies. Policy and advocacy responsibilities include: assisting with coordinating the HAN Aligning to Advance Policy initiative group; helping organize the HAN annual Policy Day; researching, analyzing, and writing policy documents; and government relations work.

Qualifications: a graduate degree or 5+ years of post-college work experience or relevant specialized skills/experience (7+ years for the manager position); proficiency in policy advocacy and communications including writing press releases and op-eds; proficiency in project management; and skilled and accomplished writing ability. Note: the posting explicitly requests that application materials not be generated by AI tools; AI use for proofreading or formatting is acceptable but materials should primarily represent the applicant's own ideas, analysis, and writing. The position requires residency in the Nashville-Davidson County Metropolitan Statistical Area; candidates outside Tennessee must relocate prior to start. Priority application deadline: August 21, 2026. At least two years of experience in public policy advocacy and research at state or local levels preferred. J.D. or graduate degree in public policy preferred but not required.

Key responsibilities include: advancing ACLU-TN's legislative and public policy agenda at the state, city, and county levels; researching and analyzing local, state, and national laws and policies affecting Tennessee communities; helping develop and implement lobbying and advocacy strategies before the Tennessee General Assembly, governor's office, and other governmental bodies; supporting legislative advocacy during legislative sessions (typically January-April) including tracking and analyzing legislation, preparing and delivering testimony and briefing materials, and meeting with lawmakers and legislative staff; building relationships with government officials, community leaders, allied organizations, and lobbyists; representing ACLU-TN in community settings, working groups, and stakeholder groups; and maintaining accurate, organized records of advocacy activities, legislative calendars, and advocacy timelines.

Qualifications: at least two years of experience in public policy advocacy and research at state or local levels preferred; demonstrated commitment to civil rights and civil liberties consistent with ACLU-TN's mission; excellent policy analysis, research, and written and oral advocacy skills; J.D. or graduate degree in public policy preferred but not required; experience with legislative procedures, bill drafting, and policy development; familiarity with the Tennessee political landscape and legislative process; and ability to work irregular hours especially during legislative session.
